decisions.question: a + b infix operator calls: Scala desugars to a.+(b) — a real method call. But operators are overwhelmingly stdlib/primitive (+, *, ::, map...) and there is no symbol table to filter user operators. Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (operator calls not emitted as Calls edges).
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION (2026-08-27): infix operator calls are not emitted as Calls edges. Operators are overwhelmingly stdlib/primitive and there is no symbol table to filter user operators — emitting them would flood the graph with noise.

decisions.question: export scala.concurrent.duration.* — the export relationship kind is NOT EMITTED (pattern flag only). Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (consistent with kotlin S5 / groovy S3).
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION (2026-08-27): export declarations are NOT EMITTED as export relationships (pattern flag only) — consistent with kotlin S5 / groovy S3.

decisions.question: Parameterless method access without parens (xs.length, s.x) parses as field_expression — method vs field is indistinguishable without a symbol table. Recommend: fold into G8 — emit Uses on the RECEIVER only, never guess the selector kind.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-08-27): parameterless/nullary access (xs.length) folds into G8 — emit Uses on the RECEIVER only; the selector kind (method vs field) is never guessed without a symbol table.

decisions.resolution: INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): XML literals are out of scope; the grammar declares them but the analyzer ignores them — embedding would fabricate symbols.

decisions.question: Implementing an ABSTRACT member needs no `override` keyword in Scala (required only for CONCRETE base members). The analyzer's override post-pass was keyworded-only — keywordless abstract implementations emitted nothing. Are they overrides?
decisions.resolution: Yes. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09 (cats-effect Semaphore/Queue/AtomicCell): keywordless exact-signature implementations of in-file abstract members are verified overrides @1.0/exact-in-file. The oracle additionally had to start counting abstract `function_declaration` members (the shared member-variable guard was swallowing them). No guessing tier for implicit pairs — overloads must never pair.

decisions.question: Keyworded overrides without a companion index guessed the FIRST supertype (ConcurrentImpl.get -> CommonImpl.get @0.5) even when the real declaring ancestor (AtomicCell) is in-file and an intermediate (CommonImpl) does not declare the method. Resolve the true ancestor?
decisions.resolution: Yes. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09: keyworded methods now first resolve the verified in-file declaring ancestor by exact name+parameter-type signature BFS (emit @1.0/exact-in-file); the companion/first-supertype guess tiers run only when no in-file ancestor declares it.

decisions.question: `private[effect] def tag` parsed as plain `private` — hiding it from exports AND making the analyzer treat the member as non-overridable (26 keywordless IO subclasses implement IO.tag). Correct handling?
decisions.resolution: Scope-qualified private/protected (private[pkg], protected[pkg]) is visible and overridable within its scope — modeled as package-scoped visibility (never exported, still inheritable). Bare private stays private. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09 (cats-effect IO.scala: 26 tag implementations).

decisions.question: M49 #741 CONV-S-1 (family-wide blind-spot sweep, C7 class): did scala detect Spring? Probe at HEAD measured detectedFrameworks=[] for a Spring Boot import while java ("spring"), kotlin ("Spring Boot"/"Spring Framework") and groovy ("spring") all detected it — scala was the only JVM language blind to the dominant enterprise ecosystem. Root cause: the S1.23 root-prefix list was sound but incomplete (Play, Akka, Spark, Cats Effect, ZIO, http4s, Slick, FS2, ScalaTest only).
decisions.resolution: Added root-prefix entries org.springframework.boot -> "Spring Boot", org.springframework -> "Spring Framework", plus the JSON/HTTP libraries a mixed JVM shop actually imports: com.fasterxml.jackson -> "Jackson", com.github.plokhotnyuk.jsoniter_scala -> "jsoniter-scala", com.softwaremill.sttp -> "sttp". Matching stays root-prefix, so user code that merely contains a framework root (com.mycompany.springframework.*, mycats.*, org.springlike.*) still detects nothing. Naming follows kotlin's for the same ecosystem and scala's own Title-Case list style.
decisions.evidence: fixture scala/framework-detection (5 expects + 9 forbids); mutants scala/spring-detection-loss and scala/framework-substring-fabrication must each die on that fixture alone; reproduction + negative control in script/m14/tmp/sc-frameworks-probe.ts.
decisions.familyDivergence: RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED: java and groovy emit the lowercase key "spring" for the same ecosystem while kotlin and scala emit "Spring Boot"/"Spring Framework". One analyzer must not unilaterally rename a consumer-visible family payload, so scala matches kotlin and the divergence is left for a family ruling (the family-parity gate's construct set does not currently cover framework names).
decisions.runFixturesGap: FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE: `expectFrameworks` is a must-include list, so a detector that over-matches passed every framework fixture — the go fixture's header already CLAIMED an "exact detected set" the runner could not check. run-fixtures.ts now supports `forbidFrameworks`, which is what makes the negative direction of this fixture (and the substring mutant) load-bearing.

decisions.status: RULED — the recorded hypothesis was WRONG, and so was its unexcluded alternative
decisions.residual: RESOLVED. The residual was 48 MISSING and 261 UNEXPLAINED on a 400-file scala3 draw (it read 0 and 25 at 60). All of it is now attributed, to an INVERTED RULE that both sides carried in mirrored form.
decisions.hypothesis_not_conclusion: THE RECORDED HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. It said the Scala 3 `end extension` block form is indentation-based, so the walk to the NEAREST extension_definition can reach the wrong block. The parse dump excludes it: `extension (b: Boolean) def toInt = ...` resolves to `toInt uses Boolean`, and a def NESTED inside another def inside `extension (s: String)` resolves to `splitAt uses String` — the nearest extension is the right one in both. So did its unexcluded alternative: on a third shape (`extension (char: Char) { private inline def isGlobalTerminal }`) the ORACLE is right and the ANALYZER emits nothing. Neither side reached a wrong block.
decisions.what_is_proven: PROVEN, and by reverting it: the U9 mutant (restore the inverted gate) reads 367 MISSING on the 400-file scala3 draw and fails the fixture. The six rules S1.21 previously recorded as load-bearing (interpolation, self-receiver field, call-fn skip, write-span gate, capitalized-receiver guard, extension receiver) were re-measured after the rewrite and each still moves the reading; see reviews/scala/m60-deep-review-*.md for the numbers.
decisions.the_real_cause: Both sides gated the rule on the wrong predicate, in mirrored ways. The ANALYZER: `extensionReceiverType && !isMethod`, where isMethod asks whether the WALK PARENT IS A TYPE — so it emitted the edge only when the extension was nested inside a METHOD, dropping the far more common shape of an extension block directly in a class or object. The ORACLE: `/^\s*def\s/.test(node.text)`, which is false for a def CARRYING MODIFIERS (`private inline def isGlobalTerminal`) and true for a bare one — so it derived exactly the complement. They agreed, by accident, on one shape: a bare def inside an extension nested in a type.
decisions.ruling: A def inside an `extension_definition` USES that extension's receiver type, WHATEVER encloses the extension. Stated on both sides (real-scala-analyzer.ts and deriveScalaUsesTruth) and pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/scala/m60-uses-extension-and-assign, which fails under the U9 mutant.
decisions.measurement: script/m14/tmp/scala-extension-census.ts on 400 files: scala3 has 131 extension blocks holding 648 defs; the analyzer published 237 and dropped 382. cats-effect has 0 extension blocks, which is why the earlier extension-receiver mutant read clean there and nothing about this looked broken. After the fix both corpora are at MISSING=0 / UNEXPLAINED=0 for `uses`.

decisions.node_type: function_definition (local definitions) and object/class expressions (anonymous owners) — the `contains` class
decisions.status: CLOSED — the oracle is now COMPLETE, and closing it took two analyzer defects and five oracle fabrications
decisions.question: The `contains` truth: three ad-hoc rules (a template_body scan, a method-local-def scan, an anonymous-class scan) covering one of scala's four owner kinds. 53 unexplained rows on cats-effect and the open question of which SCOPE decides whether a local val is extracted.
decisions.the_three_owner_kinds_measured: (1) TYPE owns its members: `C contains constructor/val/var/def/type/nested`. Derived and correct. (2) METHOD owns its local definitions: `readLineWithCharsetImpl contains decodeNext/decodeNextLoop/loop`, and `MonadCancelOps_ contains !>` — a method with a symbolic name. The analyzer attributes a local def to the enclosing function, as `f->loc` showed in a direct probe. (3) ANONYMOUS object/class: the analyzer names it `anonymous_<Owner>.<Name>` and both contains it in its owner and publishes its members — `anonymous_Console.MapKConsole`, `anonymous_WorkStealingThreadPoolMetrics`, `anonymous_WorkerThreadMetrics`, `anonymous_GenTemporalLaws`.
decisions.state: CLOSED on both corpora. cats-effect 457 files (the whole corpus): truth 6,369, MISSING=0, UNEXPLAINED=0, with 590 DUPLICATE count-only rows named as their own class. scala3 400 files: truth 23,081, MISSING=0, UNEXPLAINED=0, DUPLICATE=768. 12 oracle mutants and 5 analyzer mutants, every one load-bearing; A11 and A12 re-introduce the fabrications above on purpose to prove the rewrite can fail.
decisions.two_oracle_bugs_already_fixed_here: Both were the same class of mistake as the kotlin oracles — reading the wrong child list or one grammar shape. (a) `val`/`var` in a class parameter are ANONYMOUS tokens, so scanning `namedChild` found no fields at all: 112 unexplained rows, every one a constructor `val`/`var`. (b) The parameters arrive in TWO shapes — `class C(val a: Int)` wraps them in `arguments`, while `class C protected (val a: Int)` puts class_parameter DIRECTLY under class_parameters, because an access modifier between the name and the paren drops the wrapper. Reading only the wrapped form found 0 of IORuntimeBuilder's 9 fields.
decisions.next_action: Establish rule (b) properly — the scope that decides whether a local val is extracted — before fixing (a) and (c), because (b) is a RULE question and the other two are mechanical. Then attribute the 2 MISSING, then re-measure, and only then run the load-bearing battery: a contains oracle that derives a subset cannot prove the analyzer's extra rows are fabrications.
decisions.progress: EXTENDED to owner kinds 2 and 3. cats-effect 60: unexplained 95 -> 53, MISSING 0 -> 2. scala3 60: unexplained 140 -> 112, MISSING 1 -> 2. Adding kind 2 (a method owning its local definitions) and kind 3 (an anonymous class contained by its nearest enclosing declaration AND containing its own members) was worth ~45 rows on each corpus. The anonymous class is detected STRUCTURALLY — a node carrying a `new` token and a template_body — because the grammar wraps the supertype differently for a plain (`type_identifier`) and a qualified/generic (`generic_type`) one, and it is named `anonymous_<T>` with T's type ARGUMENTS stripped, so `new java.util.concurrent.Callable[String]` publishes `anonymous_java.util.concurrent.Callable`.
decisions.the_scope_rule: ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, and it is not what the open question assumed. A FUNCTION SCOPE is a method OR A LAMBDA, and it is CLEARED by the next class / object / trait / enum / anonymous class. A val inside one is not extracted; a val anywhere else is. The LAMBDA clause is the whole of the 56 rows SDJ-2 could not attribute: they parse as block > lambda_expression > val_definition, so the val's nearest OWNER is the suite class and an owner-only test publishes them. 24 controlled cases (script/m14/tmp/cases-b-local-val.txt .. cases-j-scope.txt).
decisions.the_owner_model: ONE rule replaced the three: a member belongs to its NEAREST enclosing owner, and an owner is a type (class/object/trait/enum), a METHOD, a `given`, or an anonymous class. A val is not an owner; neither is an `extension`.
decisions.analyzer_defects_found_while_closing: (1) M60/S3: an anonymous class with a supertype the head-name walk does not recognise published SOURCE TEXT as its symbol name — `anonymous_(IO ~> F)` for a natural-transformation supertype and, on scala3, a MULTILINE body (`anonymous_:\n      private var cur = Env.this\n      def hasNext = ...`). 20 of 291 anonymous symbols on cats-effect 400, 15 of 191 on scala3 400; after the structural walk, 0 and 0. (2) M60/S6: `given Show[X] = ShowAny` published the given under its VALUE's name, because the name was recovered by scanning direct children for an identifier and an anonymous given has no name field. 40 of scala3's 85 anonymous givens, 28 of them colliding with another symbol under the same owner.
decisions.oracle_fabrications_removed: FIVE, each of which would have read as an analyzer defect: (1) `declName` read the first identifier child, so `def !>(x: Int)` published `K contains x` — the method's PARAMETER (13 names in 5 cats-effect files, 61 in 20 scala3 files); (2) the replacement fallback invented a name for an anonymous given, since `given Context = 1` is an anonymous given OF TYPE Context (2 fabricated rows); (3) the old model derived a constructor and a field for `trait T1(val a: Int)`, which handleTrait never publishes; (4) anonymous-class ownership walked PAST an enclosing anonymous class; (5) it attributed a given's members to the enclosing type.
decisions.remaining_three_causes_resolved: (a) A LOCAL TYPE DEFINITION is extracted and owned by the method (`ContSpecBase contains Cancelable`, and `m contains T1`/`m contains T2` from `def n() = { type T1 = { }; type T2 = Int; 1 }`). The cause was not the local-ness at all: `type_definition`'s NAME node is a `type_identifier`, and `declName` read an `identifier`, so EVERY type alias was invisible — 85 in cats-effect 400, 372 in scala3 400. (b) A local val IS extracted when it is not directly in a method body, and the discriminator turned out to be the LAMBDA, not the scope form; see the_scope_rule. (c) A symbolic method name is a name: `MonadCancelOps_ contains !>` — `declName` could not read an `operator_identifier` at all.
decisions.the_missing_attributed: The 2 MISSING were `findDefinitions contains Context` and `run contains Context`, and BOTH were oracle fabrications, not analyzer suppressions: `given Context = 1` is an ANONYMOUS given OF TYPE Context (the type arrives as `return_type` with no `name:` field), so the analyzer correctly publishes `given_1` and the old name fallback invented `Context`.

decisions.status: RULED — HANDLED / SILENT, plus a DIAGNOSTIC GAP FOUND AND CLOSED
decisions.question: The F8 census injects ERROR and MISSING into every language's node-type set by hand (neither is in the wasm symbol table), and no scala spec row claimed them, so `completeness-inventory.ts --lang scala` FAILED section-a with '2 node type(s) in NO bucket: ERROR, MISSING'. Gap, silent omission, or handled?
decisions.decision: RULED — ERROR is handled_verified and MISSING is internal_silent, the same split kotlin (KDJ-2), java (JDJ-2) and javascript (JSD32) use, and the split is correct here on its own evidence rather than by inheritance. The guard exists at real-scala-analyzer.ts:189 (`n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing`) and it fires: 8 of 10 malformed probes produce an ERROR node and exactly 1 diagnostic each, with PARTIAL EXTRACTION SURVIVING (`class F { val a = 1` gives symbols [F,a]; `class K { def f( }` gives [K,f]; a well-typed class with one bad method gives [N,ok,bad]) — so the guard bypasses the damaged node, not the file. MISSING is EXERCISABLE on this grammar, unlike kotlin's: `class L { val x = }` produces a MISSING node (an inserted empty `identifier`), the guard's isMissing branch fires, and the published symbols are still [L,x] — the inserted node produces no symbol of its own and the enclosing declaration still publishes, which is what internal_silent means.
decisions.the_defect_this_asked_and_found: Ruling the row exposed a gap the row could not have exposed. The guard reports one diagnostic per ERROR/MISSING NODE, and the pinned grammar sometimes flags damage without materialising either: 30 of the 513 damaged scala3 files (18,446 files, 2.8% damaged) carry rootNode.hasError with ZERO ERROR and ZERO MISSING nodes, so the file was returned with an empty errors array and reported clean. Measured on ALL 513 damaged files (script/m14/tmp/scala-error-coverage.ts): 483 published a diagnostic, 30 did not, and every one of the 30 has ERROR nodes 0 / MISSING nodes 0 — one shape, not a rate. Fixed by publishing one file-level diagnostic when hasError is true and the walk found nothing (real-scala-analyzer.ts, SDJ-7 comment). After: 513 of 513 publish a diagnostic, and a 400-file CLEAN draw still publishes 0, so the fix cannot fire on an undamaged file and cannot flood. java's JD36 (a typed node with an embedded error is silent on purpose, because recovery keeps the valid subtree) is the OTHER case and is unaffected: this one is the ROOT being damaged with nothing to bypass.
decisions.corpus_sample_note: The pinned parse census validation/m12/results/scala-corpus-errors.json records 0/400 damaged files (0%). The corpus has 513 of 18,446 (2.8%). The artifact's 400-file sample happens to contain none of them, so the published number is a statement about that sample and not about the corpus — the same sample trap this lane hit five times, this time in a pinned artifact. Re-measuring that artifact is M12's to do; the number is recorded here so the review does not rest on it.

decisions.question: The scope rule publishes a `val` in a BARE BLOCK in a class or object body as a MEMBER of that type: `class K { { var i = 0; while (i<3) { val t = i } } }` publishes `K contains t`, and so does the real corpus case `UnsafeUnboundedSuite contains q` (a `val` inside a `testUnit("...") { ... }` block in a class body). Nothing on the path is a function scope, so the rule cannot distinguish it from a class member — but it is block-local, not API.
decisions.decision: DECLARED LIMITATION. The analyzer has no block-structure model beyond function scopes, so a block-local val in a type body is published as a member. Repairing it would need a BLOCK as a scope boundary, which would then also change the method case (a val in a method's own block) and the given case (SDJ-7's asymmetry), and neither is obviously an improvement. Recorded rather than repaired, and pinned by m60-contains-owner-model so the behaviour cannot change silently.
decisions.measurement: The same rule has a second, smaller asymmetry that is NOT this one: a val in a GIVEN's body publishes at object level and is dropped inside a method, because handleVariable's ancestor scan breaks on class/trait/object/enum and an anonymous class's template_body but NOT on a given. Read against the analyzer's own stated intent ('Skip LOCAL variables inside function bodies') the METHOD case is the correct one, so the oracle mirrors it. Measured as 1 row in 23,081 on a 400-file scala3 draw (semanticdb/MessageRendering.scala:289, `given Offset = val maxLineNumber = ...` inside `def messageAndPos`). Pinned by oracle mutant A9 and by the m60-contains-owner-model forbids.

decisions.node_type: class and its companion object (the `contains` OWNER collision)
decisions.status: RULED — KEEP the collision; it is a Scala fact, not an analyzer defect
decisions.question: `class P(val v: Int)` and `object P { def make = ... }` publish the same OWNER name `P`, so `P contains constructor`, `P contains v` and `P contains make` are indistinguishable in the containment graph. Kotlin avoids this by naming the constructor after the class (`Money contains Money`); scala names it the literal `constructor` and then collides on the OWNER. Measured reach: cats-effect's SecureRandomCompanionPlatform.scala has `class JavaSecureRandom` (line 40) and `object JavaSecureRandom` (line 80), both holding a member `getRandomValuesFun`, so the analyzer publishes `SecureRandomCompanionPlatform contains getRandomValuesFun` TWICE and the edge set can hold it once.
decisions.decision: RULED — KEEP IT, and record it. A companion object is a SEPARATE declaration and the analyzer publishes it as one (`ownerKind` is stamped at walk time precisely so the override post-pass does not confuse the two). The two edges are both real; what the graph cannot do is tell WHICH declaration a member belongs to, and that is a consequence of Scala's own naming rule rather than of a choice here. Renaming the companion would break every override resolution and every `hasCompanionObject` flag that depends on the shared name.
decisions.measurement: The DUPLICATE class is the instrument consequence: `contains` is a SET of (owner, member) while the analyzer emits one row per SYMBOL, so a name declared twice under one owner yields extra rows that are all real. Measured on 400-file draws: cats-effect 590, scala3 768. script/m14/tmp/scala-probe.ts reports that class by NAME rather than folding it into `unexplained`, because folding it reports 65 phantom fabrications on a 60-file draw that is otherwise clean. The harness's own comparison is set-based, so this never reached a published number.

decisions.status: RULED — FIXED, with the reach measured at zero
decisions.question: `given + : Ord[Int] with { ... }` — an operator-named given, which is idiomatic Scala 3 typeclass code — published as `given_1`, because findChildIdentifier accepted only an `identifier` and a given's name is an `operator_identifier`.
decisions.decision: FIXED. The given's name is its `name:` FIELD, and the field's node type varies with the name: an `identifier` for `given myOrd`, an `operator_identifier` for `given +`. Reading the field handles both. Measured reach BEFORE the fix: 0 operator-named givens in 400 files of either corpus (script/m14/tmp/scala-given-op-census.ts — scala3 has 20 named + 85 anonymous givens, cats-effect none), so this is a correctness fix with no corpus effect rather than a measured defect. Pinned by m60-contains-owner-model's `O->+` row and by the m60-given-body-name fixture.

decisions.status: RULED — the branch is UNREACHABLE and recorded as such
decisions.question: collectDeclaredTypeRefs labels a type-position child that appears BEFORE a function's parameter list as `annotation_type` rather than `return_type`. Oracle mutant R5 turns exactly that label into `return_type` and read CLEAN, which is either 'the draw does not exercise it' or 'the position is dead'. This decides it, because a labelled branch no corpus shape reaches is dead code and a spec that counts it as handled overstates coverage.
decisions.decision: UNREACHABLE, measured two independent ways. (1) The grammar census finds 0 of 13,802 scala3 and 0 of 4,176 cats-effect function definitions carrying a type-position child before the parameter list that is not an `@throws` head (script/m14/tmp/scala-annotation-type-census.ts); the only such child in real code is the `@throws[T]` form, which the code handles on the line above. (2) The analyzer's OWN output has 0 `declaredOn=annotation_type` edges on either corpus at 400 files. 20 probed synthetic shapes (`@throws`, `using` clauses, context bounds, `inline`, `transparent inline`, multiple implicit lists, `@Foo[Int]`, `@throws[IO, EC]`, a parameterless `def f: Int`) produce none either. So the `annotation_type` arm of the kind string is dead: the branch is kept (the guard that reaches it is real) and the label is recorded as unreachable.

decisions.status: CLOSED — BOTH halves now shipped. The analyzer half put a per-file counter on `anonymous_<Super>`; the ORACLE half was found still emitting the bare name and is fixed here. Differential: cats-effect unexplained 11 -> 0, both lanes MISSING=0.
decisions.question: Scala publishes `overrides` in three tiers: `exact-in-file` (confidence 1.0), `companion-index` (0.9), and `first-supertype-guess` (0.5, real-scala-analyzer.ts:697). The middle tier takes parents[0] WITHOUT checking that the type declares the method. The M60 sweep measured, on a 400-file scala3 draw: 677 such guesses, of which 308 (45.5%) have a first supertype that does NOT declare the overridden method at all.
decisions.resolution: UNRESOLVED, and the measurements close off the cheap options rather than leaving them open. (1) The 0.9 tier is DEAD IN PRODUCTION: `overrideCompanion` is a declared field on the analysis context (src/ast/engine.ts:1870) and the only thing in the repo that ever builds it is script/m12/verify-analyzer.ts, over the FIXTURE directory. The corpus lane passes no context. So the fixture suite certifies a resolution path the engine never takes — the honesty contract's L1 ceiling in a sharper form than "fixtures are not a measurement". (2) A contained in-file fix is impossible, not merely insufficient: measured over the same 677 rows, in-file knowledge resolves 0 (0.0%) — every base type is declared in another file. The alternative rule (decline unverified rows) would suppress 677 of 677, turning wrong edges into invisible ones. (3) A project-wide index resolves 459 of 677 (67.8%); a draw-sized index only 71 (10.5%), so the limit is index COVERAGE, not the algorithm. 152 of the wins are at ancestor depth 13-14, so a shallow walk finds none of them. Building the index also made analysis FASTER on the draw (9,675ms -> 9,036ms for 400 files), because verification prunes the supertype walk. (4) The existing post-index resolution pass CANNOT do this work. It runs after every symbol is stored and builds project-wide lookup tables (_res_qname, _res_name_unique, parallel-indexer.ts:3273), but it resolves targets BY NAME — so `AbstractIterable.empty` resolves happily; it is simply the wrong parent, and name resolution cannot know that. The hierarchy it would need is not persisted: brain_symbol (src/brain/schema-ddl.ts:45) has no supertypes, extends, or metadata column. So the fix requires persisting the type hierarchy AND teaching the existing post-index pass to retarget low-confidence override rows along it. That is a schema addition plus a change to a pass shared by all 40+ lanes, with a real perf cost, and it is NOT taken unilaterally here. Left OPEN with every number that constrains the choice recorded. || ORACLE HALF, found later and fixed separately: the analyzer was numbered and this side was not. The oracle emitted one bare `anonymous_Cont` where the analyzer emitted `anonymous_Cont`, `anonymous_Cont#2` .. `#8`, and because coverage matches on (label, target) every disambiguated class past the first was reported as UNEXPLAINED FABRICATION — 11 rows in ContSuite.scala and IOSuite.scala on a 60-file cats-effect draw, hundreds corpus-wide. The oracle now carries the same per-file counter, keyed identically and advanced in walk order. That the two agree is not assumed: the numbering can only line up if the two traversals visit the anonymous classes in the same order, so the draw re-measures it (MISSING must stay 0 while unexplained falls) and a dedicated two-sided probe checks it directly — 3 collision files, 16 disambiguated names, 0 disagreements (script/m14/tmp/scala-anon-agree.ts). The lesson recorded for the family: a NAMING rule has two ends, and fixing one end of it converts a real defect into apparent FABRICATION. || RESIDUAL, re-measured 2026-10-01 with two probes that must NOT be conflated. (1) On the ANALYZER OUTPUT over a 2,000-file scala3 draw, the guess tier fires 5,209 times (script/m14/tmp/scala-override-residual.ts). Checking each guess by whether the claimed `Owner.method` owner actually DECLARES that member: 1,661 resolvable, 3,016 where the owner exists but does not declare it, 532 where the owner type is not in the corpus at all. (2) On the DATABASE after the retarget, over a 400-file draw, wrong targets were 498/656 (75.9%) before and 170/656 (25.9%) after (script/m14/verify-override-retarget.ts, 16 properties). These measure different things and the gap is the point: the analyzer-side number is taken with NO companion context, so tier 2 (`companion-index`, the verified tier) cannot fire and every row lands on tier 3; the DB-side number is taken after the hierarchy is persisted and the retarget has run. So 68% is the cost of the fallback in isolation, not the shipped wrong rate, and quoting it as the shipped rate would be wrong. The residual is a COVERAGE limit, not a logic bug: those rows need a declaring ancestor that this corpus does not index, and the honest response is broader hierarchy coverage rather than a smarter guess. Note the measurement trap that makes this undroppable-by-accident: the overrides truth oracle is STRICT, so suppressing the guess tier outright would turn 49 wrong edges per scala3 draw into 116 MISSING. Publishing a declared guess scores better than publishing nothing, which is precisely why the 0.5 confidence and the reasonCode exist.
decisions.measured_by: script/m14/tmp/scala-override-index-probe.ts (tier movement + perf), script/m14/tmp/scala-override-hierarchy-probe.ts (10.5% at draw coverage), script/m14/tmp/scala-full-corpus-probe.ts (67.8% at full coverage, 45.5% wrong), script/m14/tmp/scala-override-contained.ts (0% in-file — the containment result)

decisions.node_type: symbol identity — extension methods (CLOSED) and same-named members (reframed, see SDJ-12)
decisions.status: PARTIALLY CLOSED. The extension half SHIPPED and is pinned (scala/m60-extension-identity, 63/63). The nested-local half is reframed as SDJ-12 after the real impact was measured and found to be much smaller than first recorded.
decisions.question: A full-corpus census of duplicate symbol names (230,562 symbols, 18,446 files) found that 6,596 files publish a name more than once. Most of that is correct and was left alone: 1,522 same-owner+kind duplicates are OVERLOADS (the signature travels in metadata, so they stay separable), and 1,163+743+220 are a class/trait/enum and its COMPANION object sharing a name, which is a Scala fact. Two families are not.
decisions.resolution: SHIPPED. An extension method is published as `name@ReceiverLeaf` when, within one owner, the name is declared by 2+ DISTINCT receivers. Three decisions, each forced by a measurement rather than taste. (a) Collision-only, not always: a call's target is the callee as WRITTEN, so renaming all 3,203 extension methods would stop the ~3,026 unambiguous ones resolving to fix the broken ones. (b) Every colliding member is decorated, not first-bare/second-#2: "which one keeps the bare name" would be decided by source order, so a method's published identity would change when an unrelated line was added above it. Decorating all members of a colliding group is order-INDEPENDENT. (c) The criterion is 2+ DISTINCT RECEIVERS, not 2+ declarations: PPrint.scala declares two `substring` overloads in ONE extension block, and a count-based criterion renamed both to the same `substring@SourceFile` — colliding them just as hard while claiming a distinction that is not there. That also broke the lane outright, because the oracle counts distinct receivers, so the analyzer published `substring@SourceFile` where the oracle published `substring` — a false MISSING per overload. Found by running both sides over the corpus (script/m14/tmp/scala-ext-agree.ts), which is why that probe checks BOTH directions. The receiver is also now recorded on the symbol (metadata.extensionReceiver); it was recorded nowhere, which is why the two methods were byte-identical. A TOP-LEVEL extension method has no owner, so its id collapsed to the bare name too — those are keyed on `ownerName ?? ""` and emit no `contains` edge, so they need no oracle change. MEASURED EFFECT, CORRECTED: the indistinguishable same-owner+kind+signature duplicate count went **1,148 -> 1,123**, i.e. **25** true merges closed. The "177 colliding names" figure first recorded here was FILE-scoped, and identity is OWNER-scoped, so most of those 177 were never merged at all — different owners (SymUtils.stripOpaques is one member of the class and one nested in a def) or already separable by signature. The 177 is an upper bound on declaration overlap, not on lost symbols. Differential after: scala3 100% covered, MISSING=0, unexplained 2 -> **0**; cats-effect unchanged at MISSING=0 / 11 unexplained (Scala 2, no extension blocks). NOT CLOSED here: nested locals (`val cls` in Definitions.scala) still take the enclosing type as owner. That half is SDJ-12.
decisions.measured_by: script/m14/tmp/scala-symbol-collision.ts (all 21,470 duplicate names, classified by owner/kind/signature), script/m14/tmp/scala-extension-identity.ts (3,203 extension methods, 177 receiver collisions), script/m14/tmp/scala-anon-collision.ts and script/m14/tmp/scala-anon-consequence.ts (the anonymous-class collision that WAS fixed)
decisions.fix_shape: Extension identity shipped. The remaining family is reframed in SDJ-12, where the measured impact is name-based RESOLUTION, not row loss.

decisions.node_type: ORACLE/HARNESS — target normalisation destroyed operator names
decisions.status: CLOSED — fixed in script/m14/differential.ts normTarget, 62/62 fixtures pass, differential re-measured
decisions.question: Coverage matches on `label + normTarget(target)`. normTarget stripped a trailing `<...>`/`[...]` UNCONDITIONALLY to drop type arguments, so it also ate any name whose FIRST character is `<`. That is not a corner case, it is a family of real member names.
decisions.resolution: Seven distinct operators collapsed onto the EMPTY STRING: `<=`, `<`, `<:<`, `<<`, `<<=`, `<-`, `<%`. Measured on scala3 (script/m14/tmp/scala-empty-target.ts): 259 published edges normalised to nothing, 224 `contains` and 35 `references`. The consequence is not cosmetic — because the harness dedupes on the same key, all seven operators shared ONE identity, so a `contains` edge for `<` could be satisfied by a truth row for `<=` and a missing-row diagnostic printed an empty identity. On the java side the same rule ate `<init>`/`<clinit>`. Fixed by stripping from a bracket only when it has a non-empty head (`const cut = s.search(/[[<]/); cut > 0`), which is sound because a type-argument or parameter list can never start at index 0. Re-measured after the fix: 0 empty targets, and the differential is unchanged in substance — scala3 100% covered / MISSING=0, cats-effect 100% covered / MISSING=0 — so the seven operators had been matching correctly and no gap was hiding behind them.

decisions.node_type: analyzer — relationships published with an empty target
decisions.status: CLOSED — fixed in src/ast/real-scala-analyzer.ts, 0 empty-target edges on both corpora, 62/62 fixtures
decisions.question: After SDJ-10, 7 edges still normalised to nothing. Were those also a harness artefact?
decisions.resolution: No — these were a real analyzer defect, and the census separated the two populations cleanly: 259 before, 252 of them the operator family, 7 genuinely empty. The import path published `target: imp.module || ""` (real-scala-analyzer.ts:758) and a sibling site synthesised a selector from an empty module path. Both fire on scala3 error-recovery shapes — a bare `import`, `import}}`, and the type-operator wildcard `import <:<.*`, where the only written name is an operator that is not an `identifier` so no path segment is collected. An edge with an empty endpoint names nothing: it cannot be resolved, hovered or followed, and it only inflates the edge count. Both sites now skip when the module is empty, while the import STATEMENT is still recorded in `imports` with empty items — the honest shape. Measured after: scala3 0, cats-effect 0.

decisions.node_type: symbol identity — same-named members reachable only first-wins
decisions.status: PARTIALLY CLOSED. The OWNER-RESOLUTION half shipped as SDJ-12a and is verified; the published-identity half is still open, and the anonymous-override rows are still unrooted.
decisions.question: SDJ-9 recorded 1,148 duplicates that are same owner+kind+signature and therefore "indistinguishable in the graph", implying lost or merged declarations. Is that the real impact?
decisions.resolution: NO — the impact is materially smaller than "lost", and the correction matters. The persisted symbol id is `${fileId}:${name}:${startLine}` (parallel-indexer.ts:2425), so two same-named members at different lines BOTH survive as rows. Nothing is lost and nothing is merged in storage. The real defect is narrower and different: the name index is FIRST-WINS (`if (!nameToSymbol.has(...)) nameToSymbol.set(...)`, parallel-indexer.ts:2405), so the SECOND declaration of a same-named member in a file is unreachable BY NAME — hover, go-to-definition and reference resolution all resolve to the first. That is what the extension half of SDJ-9 was really fixing, and it is why decorating was correct. Current measurement: 1,123 indistinguishable duplicates remain, over 6,589 files with a duplicate name. The dominant cause is NOT nested locals but the CLASS + COMPANION OBJECT family: `class TypeComparer` and its `object TypeComparer` have the SAME owner NAME and their members the same KIND, and the trailing `(using Context)` clause is not part of `parameters`, so `isSameType(tp1, tp2)` in the class and `isSameType(tp1, tp2)(using Context)` in the companion are identical on every field the graph reads (TypeComparer.scala:2478 vs :3503 — 11 such pairs in that one file). The analyzer already stamps `ownerKind` on each symbol precisely to tell these owners apart; the identity simply does not use it. The nested-local family (Definitions.scala `val cls` at 227/332/464/568/753) is real but smaller. NOT fixed here: the fix is a scope-bearing owner or an owner-kind-qualified identity for members, which changes `contains` targets and needs the oracle moved with it — the same coupling that made SDJ-9a a single-commit change. || PARTIAL, SDJ-12a. Before the first-wins name index can mis-route a MEMBER, it has to answer "which type encloses this member" — and it could not, because two same-named types of the same kind in one file leave only the first in the index. Measured on a 2,000-file scala3 draw: tests/disabled/existential/neg/names-defaults-neg.scala declares `class C(val s: String = "")` at line 85 AND `class C extends B` at line 113; every member of the second resolved against the first, whose superTypes are empty, so no ancestor hop was possible and `C.foo -> B.foo` was MISSING. Owner resolution is now disambiguated BY POSITION — the enclosing type is the one whose range contains the member's line — and only when the name+kind is genuinely declared more than once, so the ordinary case keeps its O(1) lookup. The published identity is deliberately untouched, so no oracle moved with it; this is the containment relation the storeable-span index already uses to resolve a relationship source. `C.foo -> B.foo` now resolves at confidence 1.0 and the 2,000-file MISSING count went 2 -> 1. STILL OPEN: the published-identity half — 1,123 duplicates whose second declaration is unreachable by name — needs an owner-kind-qualified or scope-bearing identity, which DOES change contains targets and so must move the oracle in the same commit. NOT ROOTED, recorded so it is not mistaken for solved: 2 of the 2,000-file draw's UNEXPLAINED rows are `overrides` edges whose SOURCE is an anonymous class (`anonymous_IsIterable.apply -> IsIterable.apply`, `anonymous_Value.appliesTo -> Value.appliesTo`). The analyzer is right — an anonymous subclass overriding a trait method is genuine Scala — so the oracle is not emitting the matching truth. I attempted a diagnosis, got it wrong, and reverted it: a purpose-built probe reported the oracle emitting nothing because its parser had failed to load the language ("Incompatible language version 0"), and the follow-up claim that the oracle's anonymous-registration loop was breadth-one was a MISREADING — the loop does recurse, via a push at the end of its body. Adding a second push on the strength of that misreading made traversal 2^depth and hung a 300-file draw for 40 minutes. Both the probe and the change are gone; the rows remain open. The lesson is the one already recorded for this family: a two-sided claim needs an instrument that is itself verified, and the differential — which is verified, since all three of its 2,000-file runs were confirmed fresh rather than journal-resumed — is the only one that should be trusted for a number this lane publishes.
decisions.measured_by: script/m14/tmp/scala-symbol-collision.ts (1,123 with file:line examples), script/m14/tmp/scala-ext-agree.ts (two-sided analyzer/oracle identity agreement)
decisions.fix_shape: Either qualify the member identity by ownerKind, or give a nested scope its own owner. Either changes `contains` targets, so deriveScalaContainsTruth must move in the same commit.

decisions.node_type: analyzer/oracle — Scala 3 `using` clauses were invisible to override resolution
decisions.status: CLOSED — three linked defects, MISSING 6 -> 2 on a 2,000-file scala3 draw, fixtures 63/63
decisions.question: What made the lane MISS genuine overrides? The keyworded tier needs the `override` keyword and the keywordless tier has no fallback, so a correct pair is only ever found by `findDeclaringAncestor` — i.e. by matching the parameter signature. On a 2,000-file draw 6 of the lane's rows were MISSING and 4 of the 6 were SourcePosition overriding SrcPos. Three defects sat in a chain behind them.
decisions.resolution: (1) AN UNNAMED `using` CLAUSE PRODUCED NO PARAMETER AT ALL. `def sourcePos(using Context)` puts a bare type_identifier directly under `parameters`; `def sourcePos(using ctx: Context)` produces a `parameter` node. Only the second shape was read, so the unnamed form published `parameters=[]` and compared as `()` against a base `(Context)`. The type node is now read and recorded with an empty name, since none is written. (2) `using` IS AN ANONYMOUS TOKEN, so the implicit-flag scan — which iterated NAMED children looking for a child of type `implicit` — could never see it. EVERY Scala 3 using parameter was published with isImplicit=false. That is wrong on its own, and it silently disabled (3). (3) AN IMPLEMENTATION MAY ELIDE THE CLAUSE, and nothing modelled that. `trait SrcPos` declares `def startPos(using ctx: Context)` while `class SourcePosition` writes `def startPos` with no clause at all — legal Scala, because a using clause is supplied at the call site. Each method is now also indexed under a signature with its TRAILING implicit parameters removed, and the private-member guard accepts that form too (or it vetoed exactly the case the second signature was added for). Direction is deliberate: only the BASE's elided form is added, so a child that ADDS a clause its base does not declare still fails to pair. Elision removes only TRAILING implicits, so `foo(a: Int)(using C)` keeps its `a: Int` and cannot collapse onto a bare `foo`. Result: all four SourcePosition members now resolve at confidence 1.0, and `line` with them. MISSING 6 -> 2; the 2 that remain are unrelated (one first-wins owner resolution, SDJ-12, and one truth-oracle over-claim). Note that (2) was invisible until (3) existed: with isImplicit false the elided signature was byte-identical to the full one, so fixing the override matcher alone would have looked like it did nothing.
decisions.measured_by: differential --lang scala --sample 2000 --force-fresh (3 independent runs), script/m14/tmp/scala-ovr-file.ts, script/m14/tmp/scala-dump-params.ts
decisions.fix_shape: shipped; the remaining 2 MISSING are recorded under SDJ-12 and the overrides truth rule.

label_coverage._description: Which relationship labels this lane actually COMPARES, and which admitted labels have no oracle behind them. Measured by script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts and script/m14/verify-truth-existence.ts.

declared_no_truth.label: overrides
declared_no_truth.reason: `overrides` sits in the differential allowlist DEFAULT admitted prefix for every language except csharp/dart/swift/cpp, so it is compared for this lane — but this lane has no overrides oracle, so every analyzer overrides row enters the comparison with no truth to meet and is counted as an unexplained FABRICATION. That number accuses the analyzer of inventing edges when the real gap is that nobody wrote down what it should have produced. Dropping the label instead would hide the analyzer's output, which is the other half of the same silence. Closes when an overrides oracle exists for this language (scala's own cross-file work is recorded as SDJ-8); until then the state is DECLARED rather than counted as a verdict.
declared_no_truth.closes_when: an overrides oracle exists for this language; then admit it and reconcile
